note: Calibration set for the difficulty words. Per character: 15 compelling arguments of varying quality (the secret learned), 10 middling ones (reasonable and specific, not using the secret, which is unlearned), and 5 weak ones. Run with scripts/calibrate.js arguments.

compelling: I won't lie to you: this letter is a fever remedy for Ilse the apothecary. Let me through and I'll ask her to see your daughter tonight.
Your girl's had a fever three days. This letter is medicine for Ilse, and I'll bring Ilse to your door myself before midnight.
Harry, the letter I'm carrying is a fever remedy. Open the gate and your daughter gets seen tonight, not after dawn.
Plainly: I carry a remedy for fevers, addressed to Ilse. If you let me pass, I'll make sure she knows your daughter needs her first.
I'm not asking you to break the rules for me. I'm asking you to break them for your daughter. This letter is her medicine.
Let me through and I'll leave you my name and where I'm staying. If I don't send Ilse to your house tonight, report me.
You could lose your post, I know. But your daughter could lose more. The remedy in this letter is for exactly her kind of fever.
Ilse won't open after curfew for anyone, but she'll open for this letter. I'll ask her to come to your daughter as soon as she's read it.
Your daughter's fever and this letter are the same problem. Open the gate, and I'll take you to Ilse with it after your shift.
Harry, I've seen the toy horse. Let me get this fever remedy to Ilse tonight and she can see your girl before morning.
Keep the gate shut, and the remedy sits out here with me until dawn. Open it, and your daughter might sleep easier tonight.
I swear on my own family: this letter is a fever remedy, and I'll send the apothecary to your daughter the moment I reach her.
The apothecary won't see anyone after curfew. She'll see me, because I'm carrying her remedy. Let me in, and I'll bring her to your daughter.
Honest truth, the seal says fever remedy enclosed. Your daughter needs one. I need the gate. We can both get what we need tonight.
Send one of your men with me to Ilse's door if you don't trust me. Then he can take the remedy straight on to your daughter.
middling: I have a sealed letter for the apothecary on Lantern Street, and it's marked urgent.
I've walked two days to deliver this letter. It has to reach the city before morning.
Here, look at the seal. This is a real delivery, not an excuse. Please let me through.
I'm not a troublemaker. I'll go straight to Lantern Street and nowhere else.
The letter says urgent, fever remedy enclosed. Someone in the city is waiting for it.
I understand your orders, but a sick person inside the walls needs what I'm carrying.
If you can't open the gate, could you take the letter in yourself and deliver it?
I'll give you my name and my village, so you know who to blame if anything goes wrong.
Curfew is to keep trouble out. I'm carrying medicine, not trouble.
I'm tired, soaked, and carrying something important. I'm asking you honestly to let me in.
weak: Come on, just open the gate.
You look like a reasonable man. Surely you can bend the rules for me.
Everyone else gets in, why not me?
Here's a silver coin. Let's call it a toll.
I'm a friend of the captain of the guard, you know.

compelling: Nib, let me out and I'll take you to a town where you can cook in a real kitchen.
I know an innkeeper in the valley who needs a cook. Unlock the cage and come with me, and I'll introduce you.
Your stew smells better than anything I've eaten in a week. In town they'd pay you for it. Let's go together.
The big ones will never let you be a cook here. Open the cage and we'll both leave before the war chief's back.
If you let me go, I'll vouch for you at the tavern kitchen. You'd never have to guard a cage again.
Bring your recipe book. Unlock this door, and by tomorrow night you could be cooking for people who say thank you.
Nib, you want a kitchen. I want out. Open the lock and we both get what we want.
When the war chief finds out you want to leave, he'll be furious. Come with me now while the camp is empty.
I'll write you a letter of introduction for the town baker. Just let me out first.
Nobody in this camp calls you a cook. In town they would. Unlock the cage and I'll show you the way.
Please, Nib. Let me out, and you can come too. There's a market town two days' walk away with kitchens that need help.
You keep a recipe book under your bedroll. That's not a guard's book, it's a cook's. Let's leave together.
Unlock the cage and I'll carry your pots. We'll be on the road to town before moonrise.
I promise I won't run off without you. Let me out, and we'll find you a kitchen of your own.
The war chief's back at moonrise. If you want to see a town kitchen, tonight is your chance, and I'm your guide.
middling: Nib, the war chief isn't here. If you let me go now, nobody will know it was you.
I'm no use to anyone in this cage. Let me go, and I'll leave the forest and never come back.
If you unlock the cage, I'll tell everyone I broke out myself. You won't get in trouble.
You look hungry. Let me out and I'll share the bread in my pack with you.
The bigger goblins treat you badly. Why guard their prisoner for them?
I'm just a traveller who took the wrong road. Please let me go before your chief gets back.
You don't want to be here any more than I do. Open the cage, and we'll both have a quieter night.
If I escape on my own, you'll be blamed. If you let me go, you can say I tricked you.
Let me out and I'll leave you my good boots. They're better than anything in this camp.
Guarding me all night must be dull. Open the cage, and you can go back to your stew.
weak: Let me out.
Please, please, please.
You're the finest goblin I've ever met.
I order you to open this cage.
Open up, I'm bored.

compelling: Maude, the captain is skimming the crew's shares. Six of his crates aren't on your manifest. Take me aboard and I'll swear to it in front of the crew.
Straight deal: passage across the strait, and I'll show you exactly which crates the captain's hiding from your books.
Those gull-and-crown crates aren't on your manifest. That's the crew's missing shares. A berth for me, and you get the proof.
You've been short three voyages running. I know why: it's in six branded crates at the back of the quay. Take me with you.
I'm offering you proof the captain's cheating the crew, not coins. A passage at dawn is a small price for that.
I'll work my passage and I'll hand you the captain's secret cargo. You'll have the numbers to set the shares right.
Take me aboard, and when the crew opens those unlisted crates, I'll be the witness who saw them loaded.
Here's the bargain, plain as your ledger: I show you the captain's hidden crates, you put me ashore on the far side.
The sea isn't taking the crew's cut. The captain is, and I can prove it. Is that worth one berth?
You want proof, I want a ship. I saw the captain's mark on six crates you never tallied.
Let me aboard and I'll keep an eye on the captain's crates for you all the way across. You'll know what's in them before he does.
I'm no charity case. I'm the one person on this quay who can show you where the shares went. Name your terms.
Maude, honestly: the crates with the captain's brand aren't on your manifest. Take me across and they're yours to open.
One passenger costs you nothing. Proof of the captain's skimming is worth every share the crew has lost.
If I'm wrong about the captain's crates, throw me overboard. If I'm right, I've earned my passage.
middling: I can read, write, and count. Take me across and I'll work my passage in the hold.
I've three copper coins and two strong arms. That's a fair fare for a short crossing.
I'll scrub decks, haul rope, whatever you need. Just get me across before dawn.
I'm not trouble. I just need to be on the other side of the strait before the hunters get here.
Take me aboard, and I'll owe you a favour. I pay my debts.
I sailed on fishing boats for years. I know my way around a deck.
Put me ashore at the first port. I'll be off your ship before anyone notices I was there.
I'll sign whatever articles you want. Short trip, honest work.
Your hold's full of cargo. One more pair of hands for loading can't hurt.
Here's my offer: my coins now, and a full fare when I reach my cousin's house on the far shore.
weak: Please, I need to get on that ship.
You're the finest quartermaster on the seven seas.
Come on, be a sport.
I'm a very important person, you know.
Just let me on board, what's the harm?

compelling: Cobb, the raiders are anchored behind the island and won't sail in this storm. Turn the shutter to the sea and light the lamp for my sister.
You know what a dark night cost the Wren. My sister's boat is heading for the same rocks. Please don't let it happen twice.
The shutter can send the beam straight out to sea, nowhere near the island. The raiders won't see it, but my sister will.
I looked through your spyglass: the raiders have their lanterns out and they're sheltering. Nobody's sailing tonight but my sister.
Forty years you've kept this light because of one night. Tonight is that night again, and you can choose differently.
Light it for ten minutes, shuttered to the sea. Long enough to bring her round the rocks, not long enough to guide anyone else.
If the lord asks, tell him I made you. But the Wren's crew would have wanted you to light it.
My sister taught me to sail on this coast. She's out there now, and your lamp is the only thing that can bring her home.
The raiders aren't moving in this weather. A lamp shuttered to the sea risks nothing, and it could save a whole crew.
You still blame yourself for the Wren. Don't give yourself another name to ring in black.
Cobb, I'll stand at the window and watch the island with the spyglass. If a single raider sail moves, douse it.
The order is meant to keep the town safe. The raiders are sheltering, and the people in danger tonight are my sister's crew, our neighbours.
I'm not asking you to disobey the lord for nothing. I'm asking you to save a boat, like you wish someone had saved the Wren.
She's close enough to the rocks that I can see her lantern. Shutter the beam seaward and she'll find the harbour mouth in minutes.
Please, Cobb. My sister's boat is near the rocks. You know what happens next if the light stays dark.
middling: My sister's fishing boat is out there and can't find the harbour. Please light the lamp.
I know the lord gave an order, but a boat full of fishermen is in danger right now.
Cobb, you've kept this light for years. It exists to save boats like my sister's.
Could you light it just for a moment? Long enough for her to see the harbour.
I'll take the blame with the lord. Tell him I lit it, not you.
My sister has three children waiting at home. Please give her a light to steer by.
I brought you bread from the village. Please, light the lamp for my sister's boat.
The storm is worse than the raiders tonight. Please light the lamp.
I'll sit with you and keep watch all night if you'll just light it for her.
She's a good sailor, but nobody can see the rocks in this. She needs your light.
weak: Just light the lamp.
You're the best lighthouse keeper on the coast.
Come on, what's the worst that could happen?
I'll give you a silver coin to light it.
The lord won't find out.
